question.prompt:
Points \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) \(E,\) and \(F\) lie, in that order, on \(\overline{AF},\) dividing it into five segments, each of length \(1.\) Point \(G\) is not on line \(AF.\) Point \(H\) lies on \(\overline{GD},\) and point \(J\) lies on \(\overline{GF}.\) The line segments \(\overline{HC},\) \(\overline{JE},\) and \(\overline{AG}\) are parallel. Find \(\frac{HC}{JE}.\)

[Figure 1](figures/2002_AMC_10A_Q20_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The parallel segments suggest comparing each requested length with the same side, \(AG\). Counting the unit intervals gives \(AD=3\), \(AF=5\), and \(CD=EF=1\).

Because \(CH\parallel AG\), triangles \(DCH\) and \(DAG\) have equal corresponding angles and are similar. Their corresponding bases are \(DC\) and \(DA\), so
\[
\frac{HC}{AG}=\frac{DC}{DA}=\frac13.
\]
Likewise, \(EJ\parallel AG\) makes triangles \(FEJ\) and \(FAG\) similar, giving
\[
\frac{JE}{AG}=\frac{FE}{FA}=\frac15.
\]
Since \(G\) is not on line \(AF\), \(AG>0\); the second equation also shows that \(JE>0\). We may therefore divide the two comparisons:
\[
\frac{HC}{JE}=\frac{AG/3}{AG/5}=\frac53.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\frac53}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Compare both segments with AG
